review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting native-speaker review. Honduran-register unit 2 of 6 (new, course-authored; the church strand of the Honduran register). A small evangelical congregation in a Honduran village: culto, alabanza, hermano / hermana, ofrenda, anuncios, escuela dominical, "Pastor Mario". Voseo between friends and in the children's speech (esperá, mirá, contame, ¿querés?), usted to the pastor and to the elders. The sermon is a plain retelling of Matthew 14:28-31 (Peter and the water); no verse is quoted. Points for the Honduran reviewer: whether "culto" and "alabanza" are the words this congregation would say (a Catholic parish would say misa); whether the first-Sunday announcements and the "ofrenda" read naturally; the village church of wood and zinc. The unit also brings back, on purpose, the words of es-a2-2-18, es-a2-2-19 and es-a2-2-20 (the recycling pass of 2026-10-08).

sentences.text: Es domingo, y desde temprano se oye la música en la iglesia de la aldea.
sentences.english: It is Sunday, and since early the music can be heard in the village church.

sentences.text: Anoche llovió, y el camino está lleno de agua.
sentences.english: Last night it rained, and the road is full of water.

sentences.text: Nico llega a la casa de doña Marta con los zapatos mojados y llenos de polvo.
sentences.english: Nico arrives at doña Marta's house with wet shoes full of dust.

sentences.text: —Vení, cipote —dice la abuela—. Así no podés ir a la iglesia.
sentences.english: "Come here, kid," says the grandmother. "You can't go to church like that."

sentences.text: Antes, doña Marta limpió los zapatos de Nico con un trapo y le puso su camisa blanca.
sentences.english: Before, doña Marta cleaned Nico's shoes with a cloth and put his white shirt on him.

sentences.text: En el bolsillo, Nico lleva su ofrenda: dos lempiras.
sentences.english: In his pocket, Nico carries his offering: two lempiras.

sentences.text: —¿Es mucho? —le pregunta a su abuela.
sentences.english: "Is it a lot?" he asks his grandmother.

sentences.text: —Para Dios no importa la cantidad —contesta ella—. Importa el corazón.
sentences.english: "To God the amount does not matter," she answers. "The heart matters."

sentences.text: Karla y Sam los esperan en la puerta, y los cuatro caminan juntos hasta la iglesia.
sentences.english: Karla and Sam wait for them at the door, and the four walk together to the church.

sentences.text: La iglesia es pequeña, de madera y zinc, con bancas largas y una ventana abierta.
sentences.english: The church is small, of wood and zinc, with long benches and an open window.

sentences.text: Adentro hay unas cincuenta personas, y todos se saludan con un abrazo.
sentences.english: Inside there are about fifty people, and everybody greets each other with a hug.

sentences.text: —Buenos días, hermano Sam. ¿Cómo amaneció? —pregunta una señora.
sentences.english: "Good morning, brother Sam. How did you wake up?" asks a lady.

sentences.text: —Muy bien, hermana, gracias a Dios —contesta Sam.
sentences.english: "Very well, sister, thank God," answers Sam.

sentences.text: El hermano Wilmer toca la guitarra, y la hermana Rosa dirige el canto.
sentences.english: Brother Wilmer plays the guitar, and sister Rosa leads the singing.

sentences.text: Un canto es corto y el otro es largo, pero todos cantan con alegría.
sentences.english: One song is short and the other long, but everybody sings with joy.

sentences.text: Sam no conoce las palabras, así que escucha y trata de seguir la música.
sentences.english: Sam does not know the words, so he listens and tries to follow the music.

sentences.text: —Cantá, Sam, cantá —le dice Nico—. Aquí nadie se ríe de vos.
sentences.english: "Sing, Sam, sing," Nico says to him. "Here nobody laughs at you."

sentences.text: Cuando suena el último canto, la iglesia se queda callada.
sentences.english: When the last song sounds, the church falls quiet.

sentences.text: Pastor Mario abre su Biblia y lee la historia de Pedro y el agua.
sentences.english: Pastor Mario opens his Bible and reads the story of Peter and the water.

sentences.text: —Pedro quiso caminar hacia Jesús —dice el pastor—. Dio un paso, y luego otro.
sentences.english: "Peter wanted to walk toward Jesus," says the pastor. "He took a step, and then another."

sentences.text: Algunos hermanos piensan que Pedro era un loco, y otros dicen que era valiente.
sentences.english: Some brothers think Peter was crazy, and others say he was brave.

sentences.text: —Pero después Pedro miró el viento, y empezó a tener dudas —sigue Pastor Mario.
sentences.english: "But then Peter looked at the wind, and began to have doubts," Pastor Mario goes on.

sentences.text: Su error no fue caminar; su error fue dejar de mirar a Jesús.
sentences.english: His mistake was not walking; his mistake was to stop looking at Jesus.

sentences.text: Jesús no le dijo palabras duras. La respuesta de Jesús fue tomarle la mano.
sentences.english: Jesus did not say hard words to him. Jesus's answer was to take his hand.

sentences.text: —Hermanos, a veces nos pasa lo mismo —dice el pastor—. Miramos el cielo y tenemos fe; miramos el viento y tenemos miedo.
sentences.english: "Brothers, sometimes the same happens to us," says the pastor. "We look at the sky and have faith; we look at the wind and are afraid."

sentences.text: —Pero para empezar bastaba un poco de fe, y lo demás lo hace Dios.
sentences.english: "But to begin, a little faith was enough, and God does the rest."

sentences.text: Karla escribe una frase en su cuaderno, y Sam siente una pequeña sorpresa: no esperaba entender tanto.
sentences.english: Karla writes a sentence in her notebook, and Sam feels a small surprise: he did not expect to understand so much.

sentences.text: Después del mensaje, la hermana Rosa lee los anuncios.
sentences.english: After the message, sister Rosa reads the announcements.

sentences.text: —El primer jueves hay oración, el segundo hay grupo pequeño en casa de doña Marta, y el tercero hay visita a los enfermos.
sentences.english: "The first Thursday there is prayer, the second there is small group at doña Marta's house, and the third there is a visit to the sick."

sentences.text: —La oficina de la iglesia abre los martes, de dos a cuatro de la tarde.
sentences.english: "The church office opens on Tuesdays, from two to four in the afternoon."

sentences.text: La iglesia tiene gastos: la luz, el agua y el techo de zinc.
sentences.english: The church has expenses: the electricity, the water and the zinc roof.

sentences.text: Además, la familia de don Pedro tiene una necesidad grande, porque la lluvia rompió el techo de su casa.
sentences.english: Besides, don Pedro's family has a great need, because the rain broke the roof of their house.

sentences.text: —Pedimos su apoyo, hermanos —dice la hermana Rosa—. Y no pierdan la esperanza.
sentences.english: "We ask for your support, brothers," says sister Rosa. "And do not lose hope."

sentences.text: Todo está listo para la ofrenda.
sentences.english: Everything is ready for the offering.

sentences.text: Pasan dos hermanos con una bolsa, y Nico pone sus dos lempiras con una sonrisa.
sentences.english: Two brothers pass with a bag, and Nico puts in his two lempiras with a smile.

sentences.text: Somos personas distintas, de edades distintas, pero esta mañana somos una sola familia.
sentences.english: We are different people, of different ages, but this morning we are one single family.

sentences.text: Cada primer domingo del mes, las hermanas preparan un almuerzo para todos.
sentences.english: Every first Sunday of the month, the sisters prepare a lunch for everybody.

sentences.text: Desde la madrugada, doña Marta y la hermana Rosa cocinan en el patio, con el fogón y el comal.
sentences.english: Since before dawn, doña Marta and sister Rosa have been cooking in the yard, with the stove and the griddle.

sentences.text: Hay pollo con tajadas, frijoles, arroz, aguacate y cuajada, y para los niños hay baleadas con mantequilla.
sentences.english: There is chicken with fried plantain, beans, rice, avocado and fresh cheese, and for the children there are baleadas with cream.

sentences.text: —¿Cómo amaneció, hermana? —pregunta un hermano que llega tarde.
sentences.english: "How did you wake up, sister?" asks a brother who arrives late.

sentences.text: —Cheque, hermano, gracias a Dios. ¿Y usted cómo amaneció? —contesta doña Marta.
sentences.english: "Fine, brother, thank God. And how did you wake up?" doña Marta answers.

sentences.text: Cada familia trae un poco de comida o un poco de pisto para los gastos del almuerzo.
sentences.english: Each family brings a little food or a little money for the costs of the lunch.

sentences.text: Los niños llaman «el chele» a Sam, y le piden que les cuente cuentos de su país.
sentences.english: The children call Sam "the chele," and ask him to tell them stories from his country.

sentences.text: Una cipota de cinco años le pregunta: —¿Vos sos chele porque te quemó el sol?
sentences.english: A five-year-old girl asks him: "Are you a chele because the sun burned you?"

sentences.text: —No —dice Sam, y se ríe—. Soy chele desde que nací.
sentences.english: "No," says Sam, and laughs. "I have been a chele since I was born."

sentences.text: —Ahorita no quedan baleadas, pero ahorita mismo hago otra —dice doña Marta.
sentences.english: "There are no baleadas left right now, but I will make another one right away," says doña Marta.

sentences.text: Karla sirve cuajada con tajadas a un señor mayor, y él le da las gracias con la mano en el corazón.
sentences.english: Karla serves fresh cheese with fried plantain to an elderly gentleman, and he thanks her with his hand on his heart.

sentences.text: Afuera, la gente se queda a hablar bajo el árbol grande.
sentences.english: Outside, people stay to talk under the big tree.

sentences.text: Un misionero que visita la aldea llega con una maleta grande y una sorpresa para los niños.
sentences.english: A missionary who is visiting the village arrives with a big suitcase and a surprise for the children.

sentences.text: —Esperá, cipote, no abras la maleta todavía —le dice Karla a Nico.
sentences.english: "Wait, kid, don't open the suitcase yet," Karla says to Nico.

sentences.text: Dentro de la maleta hay libros, lápices y unas camisetas de colores.
sentences.english: Inside the suitcase there are books, pencils and some colored T-shirts.

sentences.text: —¿De quién son estas camisetas? —pregunta Nico.
sentences.english: "Whose are these T-shirts?" asks Nico.

sentences.text: —Son para ustedes, los niños que vienen los domingos —contesta el misionero.
sentences.english: "They are for you, the children who come on Sundays," answers the missionary.

sentences.text: Sam mira la escena y piensa en su propia llegada a la aldea, hace unos meses.
sentences.english: Sam watches the scene and thinks of his own arrival in the village, a few months ago.

sentences.text: —¿Qué estás pensando? —le pregunta Karla.
sentences.english: "What are you thinking?" Karla asks him.

sentences.text: —Pienso que ya no soy un visitante, soy un hermano más —dice él.
sentences.english: "I think that I am no longer a visitor, I am one more brother," he says.

sentences.text: —Contame cuando sepás por qué —dice ella, y se ríe.
sentences.english: "Tell me when you know why," she says, and laughs.
